case.question: I already have double-sided word cards: meanings on the front and the corresponding English words on the back. Plan two vocabulary revision activities, maximum four minutes in total. Include what to do if I make no errors.
case.expected: Use supplied reverse layout coherently; attempt then check; reset before repetition; explicit usable zero-error branch, <=240 seconds.

answer:
1. Meaning-to-word recall (120 seconds): Shuffle the cards, keep every card meaning-side up, and go through the whole stack one card at a time: read the meaning, say the English word aloud, then flip that card to check the word on the back. If a card is wrong, say the correct word aloud, put it in a separate review pile, and reset it meaning-side up. If you make no errors, deal the cards into two equal piles and run the same meaning-to-word pass once more with the full stack. Meaning-to-word recall is productive vocabulary practice, and checking each flip immediately confirms or corrects the spoken answer. In any step, if this subset is empty or too small, use available words from the original list; repeat available words as needed within that step’s allotted time.
2. Word-to-meaning check (120 seconds): Take the review pile first, then the rest of the cards, and turn every card word-side up. For each card, say the meaning aloud, flip to check the meaning on the front, and reset the card word-side up before the next one. If you make no errors, shuffle the full stack and repeat one word-to-meaning pass, saying each meaning before flipping. Word-to-meaning recall is receptive vocabulary practice, and starting with the review pile targets the items you just missed.

answer:

  - 60 seconds: Write each word on one side of a blank card and its meaning on the other, using the full word list; if the list is empty, write five words you need from memory instead. Writing both faces creates the two-sided cards the later recall needs, and the empty-list alternative keeps the step executable. In any step, if this subset is empty or too small, use available words from the original list; repeat available words as needed within that step’s allotted time.
  - 60 seconds: Lay every card word-side up, say each meaning aloud, then flip to check; if no cards remain, stop and note the list is empty. Word-to-meaning recall builds receptive vocabulary and immediate checking corrects wrong guesses.
2. Recall words from meanings (120 seconds)
  - 60 seconds: Reset every card to its meaning side up, then say the word for each card and flip to check the spelling; if no cards remain, stop and note the list is empty. Resetting restores the prompt side, and meaning-to-word recall builds productive vocabulary while checking spelling.
  - 60 seconds: Write your attempted word for each card before flipping, then compare with the card and mark mismatches; if no cards remain, stop and note the list is empty. Recording the attempt before revealing the answer shows genuine spelling errors rather than copied corrections.

  - 70 seconds: Write each word on the front of a blank card and its meaning on the back, using the full word list; if the list is empty, write five words you need from memory instead.   - 60 seconds: Shuffle the checked cards, keep them word-side up, say each meaning aloud, flip to check, and set every card back to word-side up before the next round; if no card was missed, do one extra full round instead. Word-to-meaning recall builds receptive vocabulary, and resetting all cards keeps the next round a fair test rather than a memory of positions.
  - 60 seconds: Turn all reset cards meaning-side up, say the word aloud and write it on paper, then flip to compare spelling; repeat the missed cards once, or do a full extra round if none were missed. Producing the word from its meaning trains productive vocabulary, and writing before flipping checks spelling instead of copying the answer.
